newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Education Minister Sibusiso Bengu has scaled down the planned implementation of a new "outcomes-based" school curriculum next year by half, citing funding and staff shortages in the provinces as the main reasons.

- A document proposing to put development finance institutions under the control of a new central organisation was "unanimously" rejected by the government and the managements of parastatals, the Finance Ministry said.
- A compulsory two-year postgraduate vocational training period for medical students would not come into effect in January as planned, the South African Interim Medical and Dentral Council announced.

- The Transnet tender board and Publico subsidiary ABBM Publishers are heading for a legal tussle over the process that led to the contract to publish the South African Airways in-flight magazine being awarded to Mafube Publishers.

- Welfare Minister Geraldine Fraser-Moleketi has made a partial climb-down on the implementation of her controversial child welfare benefit scheme, increasing the proposed 75 rand per month child support grant to 100 rand.
- Cuban President Fidel Castro has a net worth on a par with one of the most famous names in U.S. capitalism -- David Rockefeller, according to Forbes magazine.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Vodacom, the country's largest cellular network operator, has set a blueprint for South African industry by achieving over one billion rand in joint economic development credits since its roll-out began three years ago.
- The South African economy was still on track to meet the government's job-creation target of about 400,000 new jobs by 2000, Finance Director-General Maria Ramos said.
- A ministerial committee has backed the development of a 1.5 billion rand deepwater port and industrial development zone at Coega near Port Elizabeth.
- Gold continued its rollercoaster ride on Tuesday, losing ground again after a few days of consolidation, prompting fears the precipitous falls of the last few weeks might start again.
SAKE-BEELD
- South Africa wants to have a trade agreement with the European Union in place by November, Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin said.
- The Atomic Energy Corp and French experts have begun a project aimed at sewing up half of the world market for the use of lasers in isolating nuclear isotopes.
- Telecommunications Minister Jay Naidoo said a study for a proposed third cell-phone network was expected to show it would be viable.
THE STAR
- Police will put together a team of detectives, including a specialist in serial killings, to investigate the murders of at least seven people at Wemmer Pan, south of Johannesburg, in recent months.
